findings.claim: 020K (CODEOWNERS wiring) is entirely absent from the Track 1 slice ordering and §9 autonomous-run-complete acceptance criteria, yet 020D2 — which is in scope — depends on 020K for correct branch-protection configuration.
findings.evidence: WP-SCP-020 §3 canonical ordering: '020J [PRECONDITION for 020D1] → 020K [PRECONDITION for 020D2] → 020D1'. WP-SCP-020 §4 020K: 'Slice completes before 020D2 opens.' WP-SCP-020 §4 020D2: 'require_review_from_non_author per 020K outcome'. WP-SCP-020 §4 020B(viii-c) gate 1: 'an approving review from a member of SCP-CODEOWNERS' — CODEOWNERS must exist before this gate can fire. WP-SCP-022 §3 Track 1 ordering lists 8 slices (020B, 020B.1, 020B.2, 020C, 020C.1, 020J, 020D1, 020D2) with no 020K. WP-SCP-022 §9 autonomous-run-complete: 'Track 1 has merged … 020J → 020D1 → 020D2 to main (8 PRs)' — 020K absent from both sequence and count.
findings.impact: Without 020K, (a) no CODEOWNERS file exists so the break-glass three-gate check (020B(viii-c) gate 1) cannot validate reviewer membership, (b) 020D2 cannot correctly set `require_review_from_non_author` because its value is 'per 020K outcome', and (c) WP-SCP-020 §9 acceptance criterion 2 ('last 3 PRs show check passing') cannot be met since the branch-protection rule shape is incomplete. The autonomous chain will either run 020D2 with misconfigured branch protection or fail on the missing CODEOWNERS dependency.
findings.mitigation: Insert 020K as item 7 in the Track 1 ordering (after 020C.1/020J, before 020D1), matching WP-SCP-020 §3's canonical sequence. Update §9 autonomous-run-complete to list 9 PRs (adding 020K between 020J and 020D1). Update D-027's Track 1 sequence in docs/DECISIONS.md accordingly.

findings.claim: WP-SCP-022 places 020D2 (enable required status check) at Track 1 position 8, immediately after 020D1, inverting WP-SCP-020's canonical ordering which requires 020D1 → 020H(part1) → 020E.a → 020H(part2) → 020D2. This removes the safety gate of validating the system before enforcing it.
findings.evidence: WP-SCP-020 §3 canonical ordering (lines 83–101): '020D1 → 020H part 1 → 020E.a → 020H part 2 → 020D2 → 020E.b → 020E.c'. WP-SCP-020 §4 020H part 2: 'Promote v1.0.0-rc.1 → v1.0.0 after 020E.a green.' WP-SCP-020 §8 risk 'Bootstrap trust': 'rc.1 → v1.0.0 promotion governance = release-signoff.md named signer + canary-run-id reference' — the canary run-id (from 020E.a) must exist before v1.0.0 is promoted and before 020D2 locks down main. WP-SCP-022 §3: 020D2 at position 8 (before [USER GATE A]); 020H(1) and 020H(2) at positions 9–10 (after [USER GATE A]).
findings.impact: (a) Enabling the required check (020D2) before v1.0.0 is tagged means SCP main's enforcement references an untagged commit, not the v1.0.0 release. (b) The release-signoff.md governance record (required by WP-SCP-020 §4 020H part 2) cannot include a canary-run-id because the canary has not yet run. (c) The 'pre-protection canary' (020E.a) is semantically wrong if the required check is already active; subsequent PRs would be blocked by an unapproved check during the canary attempt. (d) USER-GATE-A's description 'Confirms self-dogfood is real before proceeding to v1.0.0 release' is correct in intent but the ordering means 020D2 has already enforced the check — the gate is after enforcement, not before the release that the enforcement depends on.
findings.mitigation: Reorder the Track 1 autonomous-run sequence to: 020B → 020B.1 → 020B.2 → 020C → 020C.1 → 020J → 020K → 020D1 → 020H(part1) → 020E.a(SCP-self) → 020H(part2) → 020D2 → [USER-GATE-A], matching WP-SCP-020 §3. Update §3 autonomous run scope to 'Track 1: through 020D2 then [USER GATE A], inclusive of 020H parts 1 and 2 and the SCP self pre-protection canary'. Update D-027 Track 1 sequence accordingly.

WP-SCP-020 §4 defines 020E.a as 'Pre-protection canary. Committed fixture branch canary/deliberate-violation-pre with deliberate Rego violation' on SCP itself.
findings.evidence: WP-SCP-020 §4 020E.a: 'Pre-protection canary. Committed fixture branch canary/deliberate-violation-pre with deliberate Rego violation; gh pr view --json dump stored; failing workflow-run-id recorded; cold-start + warm-start wall-clock times recorded (closure of m-devex-12). Evidence in canary-evidence.md.' WP-SCP-020 §4.1 deferred table: '020I → WP-SCP-020.1: FLA pilot wiring at v1.0.0 pin. Blocker: (a) FLA economical; (b) Go SDK for CT auth landed; (c) CT lessons absorbed. Not in 020 acceptance.' WP-SCP-022 §3 item 12: '020E.a — First canary: FLA pin + branch protection.' WP-SCP-022 §7: 'FLA economical — close but not absolutely there as of 2026-04-28' and 'ct-auth Go SDK specifically is still pending' — the FLA-canary prerequisites are unmet.
findings.impact: The autonomous orchestrator, reading §3's description when building the 020E.a dispatch package, will instruct Codex to perform FLA pin work on an external repo. The actual SCP self pre-protection canary evidence (canary-evidence.md with workflow-run-id, cold/warm times) will never be produced. WP-SCP-020 §9 item 3 requires this evidence. FLA pilot work (020I) was explicitly deferred; running it under 020E.a pollutes the audit trail with misidentified slice work. The stability prerequisites for FLA work are unmet (§7), so the dispatch would be doomed to fail or produce incomplete evidence.
findings.mitigation: Correct §3 item 12 to: '020E.a — Pre-protection canary on SCP self: fixture branch canary/deliberate-violation-pre demonstrates deliberate deny; workflow-run-id and cold/warm wall-clock times recorded per WP-SCP-020 §4.' If the FLA canary (020I/WP-SCP-020.1) is intended to appear post-GATE-B, assign it a distinct slice label (e.g., '020I.a') and note that it is gated on §7 stability prereqs being met at that gate.

findings.claim: Slices 020E.b (post-protection canary) and 020E.c (waiver-suppression canary) are entirely absent from WP-SCP-022's ordered slice list, silently dropping acceptance criteria required by WP-SCP-020 §9 item 3.
findings.evidence: WP-SCP-020 §9 item 3: 'All three canaries (020E.a, 020E.b, 020E.c) demonstrate expected blocking + suppression behaviour; evidence = committed fixture branches + gh pr view --json dumps + workflow-run-ids + cold/warm wall-clock times; scripts/replay-canary.sh replays all.' findings.claim: §4.3 consolidation logic does not specify the merge decision for the case where verdicts are APPROVED_WITH_FINDINGS with only MIN or nit findings (no CRIT, no unmitigated MAJ). The autonomous orchestrator has no defined behavior for this case.
findings.evidence: WP-SCP-022 §4.3: 'All three APPROVED → fixpoint reached, slice merges.' and 'Any CHANGES_REQUESTED, or APPROVED_WITH_FINDINGS where any CRIT or unmitigated MAJ exists → fix round R(F).' SonnetReviewResult schema description: 'CHANGES_REQUESTED means any CRIT present or MAJ without mitigation' — i.e., APPROVED_WITH_FINDINGS is the verdict when findings exist but none are CRIT or unmitigated MAJ. The case 'two APPROVED + one APPROVED_WITH_FINDINGS (all MIN/nit)' or 'three APPROVED_WITH_FINDINGS (all nit)' is not covered by either clause.
findings.impact: When a reviewer returns APPROVED_WITH_FINDINGS with only nit findings, the 'all three APPROVED' clause does not fire (one is not APPROVED), the CRIT/MAJ clause does not fire either. The orchestrator stalls with undefined behavior. In the worst case it defaults to triggering a fix round, consuming up to 5 rounds for nit-level findings and potentially exhausting the fix-round budget on otherwise complete slices. In the best case it crashes; either way the autonomous chain breaks.
findings.mitigation: Add an explicit rule to §4.3: 'APPROVED_WITH_FINDINGS where every finding has severity MIN or nit, with no CRIT and no unmitigated MAJ, is treated as equivalent to APPROVED for consolidation purposes. Fixpoint is reached when all three reviewers return APPROVED or APPROVED_WITH_FINDINGS(MIN/nit-only); MIN/nit findings are recorded in fixpoint.md but do not block merge.' Additionally specify: 'If at least one reviewer returns CHANGES_REQUESTED or APPROVED_WITH_FINDINGS with a CRIT or unmitigated MAJ, trigger fix round regardless of the other two reviewers' verdicts.'

findings.claim: §4.3 states fix rounds use 'resume_session_id set to the original dispatch's session id', but codex_dispatch.py's DispatcherResult output does not include a session_id field, and the plan does not specify which output field the orchestrator should extract the session_id from.
findings.evidence: codex_dispatch.py dispatch() function (lines 521–543) returns a final_record dict with keys: package_id, ts_utc_start, elapsed_seconds, timed_out, codex_exit_code, cwd, git_sha_before, git_sha_after, git_status_after, scope_violations, verify_results, verify_all_green, codex_structured_result, codex_status, effective_status, gate_failure, privsep_dispatch_token, privsep_refusal_reason, stdout_tail, stderr_tail. There is no session_id key at the top level. The codex_structured_result key holds whatever Codex returns in its final JSON. WP-SCP-022 §4.3: 'Fix round R(F) dispatches a new Codex package with the consolidated findings list and resume_session_id set to the original dispatch's session id.' codex_work_package.schema.json resume_session_id description: 'If non-null, invokes codex exec resume <id> to continue a prior session.'
findings.impact: The orchestrator cannot mechanically build a fix-round package without knowing where to find the session_id. If the orchestrator guesses or omits resume_session_id, Codex starts a new session without context, losing all prior work. The chain either stalls waiting for unspecified information or silently starts fix rounds from scratch, violating the plan's intent to continue where work left off. This failure will occur at the first fix round of the first slice that needs one.
findings.mitigation: Add a note to §4.3 specifying: 'The session_id for resume_session_id is extracted from the dispatcher result field codex_structured_result.session_id (from Codex's structured output). If this field is absent, escalate to user before triggering the fix round — do not retry without a valid session_id.' Additionally verify against the codex_dispatch_result.schema.json that a session_id field is present in Codex's structured output schema, and if not, document the alternative mechanism (e.g., ts_utc_start as a resume correlator, or a Codex-specific session extraction command).

findings.claim: §9 autonomous-run-complete acceptance criterion states 'Track 1 has merged … 020J → 020D1 → 020D2 to main (8 PRs)' but the slice count will be 9 once 020K is inserted per CRIT-01 mitigation, and the listed sequence omits 020K.
findings.impact: After CRIT-01 is fixed, the acceptance criterion's PR count '(8 PRs)' becomes factually wrong. An agent verifying completion by counting merged PRs against the criterion will mis-report the run as incomplete (9 merged but criterion says 8) or ignore 020K's merge. This creates an ambiguous completion signal at USER-GATE-A.
findings.mitigation: After inserting 020K per CRIT-01 mitigation, update §9 to: 'Track 1 has merged 020B → 020B.1 → 020B.2 → 020C → 020C.1 → 020J → 020K → 020D1 → 020D2 to main (9 PRs).' Tied to CRIT-01 fix.

findings.claim: §13 U-022-01 states '$TBD per-slice budget, $TBD aggregate' for the review-cost cap, leaving R-022-07's mitigation ('if cumulative review spend exceeds a per-WP cap') unquantified for the entire autonomous run between start and USER-GATE-A.
findings.evidence: WP-SCP-022 §13: 'U-022-01 (close before USER-GATE-A): review-cost cap for the programme. R-022-07 mitigation requires a number; default proposal $TBD per-slice budget, $TBD aggregate.' WP-SCP-022 R-022-07: 'if cumulative review spend exceeds a per-WP cap (TBD with user at user-gate A), pause.' §9 plan-complete criteria does not require U-022-01 to be closed before plan merges, so TBD values can persist into the autonomous run.
findings.impact: The chain has no budget trigger from start through USER-GATE-A. A runaway fix-round explosion (R-022-05) combined with high review costs (195 possible review dispatches per §4 calculation) would proceed uncapped. The risk is bounded by the 5-round fix budget per slice, but without a dollar ceiling the chain cannot self-pause on spend alone.
findings.mitigation: Document a concrete default cap in §13 — e.g., '$30 per-slice (all review rounds combined), $300 aggregate for the full autonomous run' — with a note that the user may override at USER-GATE-A. This closes R-022-07's open mitigation without blocking the plan merge.

The codex_work_package schema was verified by reading the file; all field names, types, and constraints in §4.1 are compatible. The package_id pattern ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$ accepts the example 'wp-scp-020b-reusable-workflow'. No additionalProperties violation detected.

The pyproject.toml partition claim ([tool.scp.federation] vs [project.optional-dependencies.mcp]) was verified against the current pyproject.toml; neither section exists yet, so both tracks add new non-overlapping sections — the conflict-free claim is correct.

I was unable to read codex_dispatch_result.schema.json (not in the review context) to confirm whether a session_id field appears in Codex's structured output. MAJ-04 is raised as a finding because the dispatcher's DispatcherResult dict demonstrably lacks a top-level session_id; the reviewer cannot rule out that codex_structured_result contains one, but the plan must specify this explicitly.

The WP-SCP-020 canonical ordering is unambiguous on the 020D1→020H(1)→020E.a→020H(2)→020D2 sequence. CRIT-02 confidence is high. The reviewer considered whether WP-SCP-022 may have intentionally reordered with valid justification (e.g., deferred release to post-gate), but found no such justification in the plan text and found that the reordering removes a governance safety valve documented in WP-SCP-020 §8.

The plan correctly identifies that 020J is a precondition for 020D1, and that 020K is a precondition for 020D2. CRIT-01 finding is supported by WP-SCP-020 §3 header annotations and §4 slice descriptions.
D-026, D-027, and D-028 are internally consistent with the plan body; they inherit the ordering errors but do not introduce additional inconsistencies beyond what is in §3 and §4.
structured_review.summary: WP-SCP-022 v0.1 has three critical ordering and description errors that would derail the autonomous chain before it reaches USER-GATE-A. First, slice 020K (CODEOWNERS wiring) is entirely absent from the Track 1 ordering and §9 acceptance criteria, yet 020D2 — which is in scope — depends on 020K outcome for its branch-protection settings. Second, WP-SCP-022 places 020D2 immediately after 020D1 (positions 7→8), inverting WP-SCP-020's canonical governance sequence (020D1→020H(1)→020E.a→020H(2)→020D2), which exists precisely to validate the system before enforcing it. Third, the description of 020E.a after USER-GATE-B reads 'First canary: FLA pin + branch protection', which conflates it with the deferred 020I FLA pilot; WP-SCP-020 §4 defines 020E.a as the SCP self pre-protection canary. Four additional major defects exist: 020E.b and 020E.c are silently dropped despite being required by WP-SCP-020 §9 item 3; 020H part 1's description wrongly includes the ADOPT-001 §12 guide (which belongs to 020H part 3); the §4.3 consolidation logic leaves the 'APPROVED_WITH_FINDINGS where all findings are MIN/nit' case undefined; and the fix-round protocol does not specify where the orchestrator extracts the session_id needed to populate resume_session_id. The schema compatibility checks (codex_work_package and sonnet_review_result) pass cleanly. The pyproject.toml partition claim is correct. D-026/D-027/D-028 are internally consistent with the plan body, though they inherit the ordering errors.
